findings.where: Hero heading, the two red Cinzel lines 'MARK · M · MOSELEY' and 'INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The name and the job title are the same size, weight, colour and tracking. The title line is much longer, so it is the widest and loudest line on the screen. The eye lands on 'INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' before Mark's name. The heading reads as one undivided band, with nothing to separate who he is from what he does.
findings.who_objects: Mark, and a development-bank officer arriving on the page. The brief says the individual is the brand (value 1, §5), so his name should lead. As set, the generic job description dominates and reads more like a firm's label than a person.

findings.where: Interpuncts in the Cinzel capitals: the hero heading and the 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED' motion heading use them, but the article headline 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW', the section labels ('TYPE PAIR', 'AN ARTICLE PAGE', 'MOTION SKETCH') and the post meta line use plain word spaces
findings.fault: The type-pair note sets a rule: Cinzel is always set with words parted by interpuncts. The tile breaks that rule in more places than it keeps it. Capital headings that should look alike are spaced two different ways, and in the meta line the interpunct is used as a separator between fields, not between words.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding a post title in Cinzel, can't tell from the tile whether to type interpuncts. The layout round will inherit a rule its own specimen contradicts.

findings.fault: The code and the file path fall back to the browser's default monospace. That adds a third, unplanned face that doesn't belong to the pair. It is also set visibly larger and heavier than the small Alegreya Sans around it, so a file path becomes the loudest thing in the note and pushes the line spacing apart.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder reading the style tile. The tile is meant to show the type pair the site will use, and the stray system face makes it look unfinished. This sits against the house guardrail on the default font stack.

findings.where: Motion sketch timeline table, the START and LENGTH columns ('0 ms', '200 ms', '700 ms', '900 ms'), and the total line ('1400 ms')
findings.fault: The timings use Alegreya Sans's old-style figures, which rise and drop below the line, and they are left-aligned. In a column of numbers the digits don't line up and the values look uneven. Tables want lining, tabular figures.
findings.who_objects: Anyone comparing the timings, such as the animation round (#9) reading off the timeline. The ragged figures make the column harder to scan.

findings.where: Article specimen at phone width, the meta line 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER / 2024'
findings.fault: The tracked capitals break the date across two lines, leaving the year alone on the second line.
findings.who_objects: A reader on a phone, who has to put the date back together. It also looks careless right under a headline.
